quiz.title: T4.2: Manipulates Lists
quiz.description: Scenario-based questions on $LISTBUILD, $LIST, $LISTGET, $LISTNEXT iteration, $LISTTOSTRING/$LISTFROMSTRING conversions, $LISTLENGTH, $LISTFIND, $LISTSAME, and list vs delimited string comparisons.

questions.question:
Consider the following list:

set x = $LB("A", "B", "C")

How do you retrieve the third element in this list?
questions.explanation: $LISTGET uses 1-based indexing. $LISTGET(x, 3, "default value") returns the element at position 3, which is "C". The third argument is a default value returned only if the position is undefined. $LISTNEXT is an iteration function with different syntax (it takes a pointer, not a position). (Reference: InterSystems Practice Q15; https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistget)

questions.question:
You are building a patient demographics record. Consider:

set record = $LISTBUILD("Smith", "John", 45, "Male")
write $LISTGET(record, 2)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTGET retrieves an element by its 1-based position. Position 2 of the list ("Smith", "John", 45, "Male") is "John". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistget)

questions.question:
A data import routine encounters missing fields. Consider:

set row = $LISTBUILD("OrderA",,"Shipped")
write $LISTGET(row, 2, "N/A")

What is the output?
questions.explanation: In $LISTBUILD("OrderA",,"Shipped"), position 2 is undefined (null) - not an empty string, but truly undefined. $LISTGET with a default value returns "N/A" for an undefined element. If position 2 were an empty string ($LB("OrderA","","Shipped")), $LISTGET would return the empty string instead. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistget)

questions.question:
You are converting data between list and delimited formats. Consider:

set colors = $LISTBUILD("Red", "Green", "Blue")
set str = $LISTTOSTRING(colors, "|")
write str

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTTOSTRING converts a $LISTBUILD list into a delimited string. The second argument specifies the delimiter character. With "|" as the delimiter, the result is "Red|Green|Blue". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flisttostring)

questions.question:
A CSV file parser needs to convert a line into a list. Consider:

set line = "Tokyo,London,Paris"
set cities = $LISTFROMSTRING(line, ",")
write $LISTGET(cities, 2)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTFROMSTRING converts a delimited string into a $LISTBUILD list. Using "," as the delimiter, "Tokyo,London,Paris" becomes $LB("Tokyo","London","Paris"). Position 2 is "London". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistfromstring)

questions.question: You need to iterate through a list of error messages as efficiently as possible. Which code is correct?
questions.explanation: $LISTNEXT requires the pointer to be initialized to 0 before the first call. Each call advances the pointer internally and sets the value in msg. It returns 1 while elements remain and 0 when exhausted. $LISTNEXT is the most efficient way to iterate because it avoids recalculating offsets. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistnext)

questions.question:
You are merging two lists of permissions. Consider:

set read = $LISTBUILD("view", "export")
set write = $LISTBUILD("edit", "delete")
set all = read _ write
write $LISTLENGTH(all)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Concatenating two $LISTBUILD lists with the _ operator produces a valid combined list. $LB("view","export") _ $LB("edit","delete") creates $LB("view","export","edit","delete"), which has 4 elements. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_lists)

questions.question:
A data correction routine needs to update a list element in place. Consider:

set items = $LISTBUILD("Apple", "Bannana", "Cherry")
set $LIST(items, 2) = "Banana"
write $LISTGET(items, 2)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: SET $LIST(list, position) = value modifies the list in place, replacing the element at the specified position. After the correction, position 2 now contains "Banana" instead of the misspelled "Bannana". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flist)

questions.question:
You need to extract a sublist from a larger list. Consider:

set weekdays = $LISTBUILD("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri")
set midweek = $LIST(weekdays, 2, 4)
write $LISTTOSTRING(midweek, "-")

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LIST(list, from, to) extracts a sublist from position 'from' to position 'to' inclusive. $LIST(weekdays, 2, 4) returns $LB("Tue","Wed","Thu"). Converting to string with "-" gives "Tue-Wed-Thu". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flist)

questions.question:
You are searching for a specific role in a user's role list. Consider:

set roles = $LISTBUILD("Admin", "Editor", "Viewer", "Auditor")
write $LISTFIND(roles, "Viewer")

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTFIND searches for an element in a list and returns its 1-based position. "Viewer" is at position 3. If the element is not found, $LISTFIND returns 0. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistfind)

questions.question:
A developer reports that accessing a null list element throws an error. Consider:

set x = $LISTBUILD("A",,"C")
write $LIST(x, 2)

What happens?
questions.explanation: Position 2 in $LB("A",,"C") is undefined (null). Unlike $LISTGET which returns a default value for undefined elements, $LIST throws a <NULL VALUE> error. Use $LISTGET with a default value to safely access elements that might be null. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flist)

questions.question: A colleague asks about the advantages of $LISTBUILD lists over delimited strings. Which of the following are true? (Select all that apply)
options: Elements can contain the delimiter character without conflict
Elements can be undefined (null) as distinct from empty string
$LISTBUILD lists use significantly less memory than delimited strings
Elements preserve their data type (string vs number)
$LISTBUILD lists can be displayed in readable $LISTBUILD notation using ZWRITE
questions.explanation: $LISTBUILD lists use a binary encoded format that preserves data types, supports null/undefined elements distinct from empty strings, and avoids delimiter conflicts. WRITE outputs the binary representation of a $LISTBUILD list (garbled characters), while ZWRITE displays them in readable $lb() notation (e.g., ZWRITE $LB("A",,"C") shows $lb("A",,"C")). Memory usage is comparable to delimited strings. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_lists)

questions.question:
You need to verify whether an incoming value is a valid list before processing. Consider:

set input = "not a list"
write $LISTVALID(input)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTVALID returns 1 if the value is a valid $LISTBUILD list and 0 otherwise. A plain string "not a list" is not a valid list structure, so $LISTVALID returns 0. This is the safe way to test before calling list functions. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistvalid)

questions.question:
You are comparing two lists that were built differently. Consider:

set list1 = $LISTBUILD("X", "Y", "Z")
set list2 = $LISTFROMSTRING("X,Y,Z", ",")
write $LISTSAME(list1, list2)

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $LISTSAME compares two lists element by element. Both list1 and list2 contain the same three string elements ("X", "Y", "Z") in the same order, so $LISTSAME returns 1 (true), even though they were constructed differently. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistsame)

$LISTFIND returns the 1-based position of the element "R05" in the list. It is at position 2. Since 2 is non-zero (truthy), the if branch executes and prints "Found at position: 2". If the element were not in the list, $LISTFIND would return 0 (falsy). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_flistfind)
